To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microfluidic chips with individually addressable electrodes can be used to concentrate, focus, and meter DNA in microchannels.

microfabricated addressable electrode arrays can be used to collect and focus biomolecules in microchannels, and that this approach is capable of concentrating samples by orders of magnitude within a small device volume.

we developed a new microfluidic technique that enables the precise handling of small volumes of charged biomolecules in a microchannel environment and demonstrated its application for the analysis of DNA samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new approach to microfluidic sample handling for portable bioanalytical applications.

the development and application of novel microfluidic technologies for bioanalysis, with a focus on the development of microfluidic devices that are capable of performing multiple operations on charged biomolecules.

the development and application of microfluidic technologies for the analysis of biological samples, with a focus on the development of portable, low-power devices that can be used in resource-limited settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of addressable electrode arrays enables precise, high-throughput sample manipulation for microfluidic bioanalysis.
this technique provides an efficient and versatile method for the collection, focusing, and injection of charged biomolecules into microfluidic channels for bioanalytical applications.
this work represents a new paradigm for sample injection, concentration, focusing, metering, and injection of charged biomolecules for bioanalysis in a microfluidic environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of individually addressable electrodes in microchannels enables the precise control and manipulation of biomolecules, which will enable the design and fabrication of portable, low-power, and low-sample-volume bioanalytical devices.
we have developed a new method to concentrate, focus, and meter charged biomolecules for bioanalysis applications.
we have developed a novel microfluidic device for DNA collection, focusing, and injection that can be used for a variety of portable, low-power, microscale bioanalysis applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to control the motion of charged biomolecules in microfluidic devices will enable new and exciting opportunities for portable bioanalysis.
microfluidic electrodes can be used to manipulate charged biomolecules in a manner that allows them to be concentrated, metered, focused, and injected into analysis channels.
this technology can be used to collect, focus, and meter charged biomolecules with high precision and reproducibility for portable, low-power bioanalysis in a variety of microchannel configurations.
